To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bioconversion of a steroid intermediate, 16‐dehydpregnenolone (16‐DHP) to the steroid hormone, androstenedione, was achieved using a mixed culture of P. diminuta and C. acidovorans, with a conversion of up to 60% in shake flasks and 45% in 5 L fermenters.
the bioconversion of a precursor of female sex hormones to an intermediate by mixed culture of two bacteria was successfully optimized.

the mixed culture of P. diminuta and C. acidovorans can be used for efficient bioconversion of 17α‐hydroxy‐pregnenolone to androsta-1,4-diene-3,17-dione, which is the precursor for the production of sex hormones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mixed culture process for the bioconversion 16‐DHA to ADD.
the optimization of the physicochemical parameters involved in mixed culture bioconversion of 6β‐hydroxyprogesterone to ADD.
the optimization of physicochemical parameters of mixed culture bioconversion for the production of ADD from 16‐D PA.

the mixed culture bioconversion of 17‐hydroxypregnenolone to 17‐hydroxyprogesterone is a viable and attractive option for commercial scale‐up of this bioconversion process.
the bioconversion of ADD to 16‐DHA by the co‐culture is an efficient, economical and eco‐friendly alternative to the conventional chemical process.
